title: mini-prober runtime: kernel-aware model routing, acceptability scoring, and graceful slowpath degradation
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: We need a lightweight speculative probe (mini-prober) that can exercise fast model candidates on a short prefix to predict whether the candidate will produce acceptable continuation. The prober must be kernel-aware (prefer variants that map efficiently to target hardware kernels), emit an acceptability score tied to quality and latency, and trigger a deterministic slowpath fallback when confidence is low. Goals: 1) reduce end-to-end latency on common queries by opportunistically routing to low-cost fast models when the prober predicts success; 2) avoid user-facing regressions by using a conservative acceptance metric and a robust slowpath; 3) ensure routing decisions account for kernel affinity and current kernel load to avoid pathological scheduling.

Design constraints: mini-prober must add <6ms median overhead for short requests, support streaming early signals, be opt-in per customer route, and integrate with existing routing policy layer.

Success criteria: 1) 10-20% tail latency reduction on targeted routes in canary traffic; 2) fewer than 0.5% quality regressions (measured by eval prompts) attributable to prober routing during rollout; 3) clear telemetry for probe accuracy, kernel-affinity mismatch, and fallback frequency.
acceptance_criteria: Prober implements a 16-token probe window and emits a numeric acceptability score (0.0-1.0)
Routing policy can consume probe score and kernel-affinity hint and make immediate model selection decision
Fallback path is exercised and verified in integration tests and can be forced via a debug flag
Canary rollout shows >=10% median latency improvement and <0.5% regression on eval suite for selected routes
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Prototype mini-prober as edge middleware that issues a parallel probe to candidate models and returns an acceptability signal back to router
Phase 2: Integrate kernel affinity tagging (kernel_fingerprint) produced by runtime selector into probe metadata
Phase 3: Expose policy knobs in routing config: probe_timeout_ms, acceptance_threshold, kernel_affinity_weight
Phase 4: Add canary gating and rollout scripts that gradually increase traffic to prober-enabled routing
Phase 5: Observability: dashboards, SLO alerts, and postmortem playbook entry
telemetry_and_metrics: probe_accept_rate (fraction of probes that cross threshold)
probe_precision/recall vs. ground-truth continuation quality over eval prompts
fallback_rate (percent of requests routed to slowpath after low confidence)
kernel_affinity_conflict_rate (probe preferred kernel != actual scheduled kernel)
risks_and_mitigations: False positives: prober mislabels low-quality outputs as acceptable -> mitigation: conservative thresholding + paired-eval checks
Kernel mismatch: probe prefers a model variant that maps poorly to current kernel -> mitigation: include runtime kernel-load in affinity score and degrade affinity weight when mismatch detected
Added overhead: probes increase load -> mitigation: sample rate limit per route and rate-limited prober threads
Operational complexity: new knobs increase cognitive load -> mitigation: sane defaults, UI tooltips, and a preconfigured 'safe' policy for enterprise routes
testing_plan: Unit tests for probe scoring logic and kernel-affinity extraction
Integration tests simulating high kernel load and verify safe fallback behavior
Synthetic A/B tests with seeded eval prompts to measure precision/recall
Canary rollout on <5% of traffic with daily quality guardrails and abort on regression
